speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a rash on your scalp and forehead; can you tell me how long you've had this symptom and if it is itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that history. Given the child's age, the seasonal nature of the rash (worsening in cold weather), and the father's history of psoriasis, could you describe exactly what the skin looks like—does it have silvery scales or greasy yellow crusts, and is there any hair loss?

REQUEST TEST: TSH, Vitamin D, CBC with differential.
REQUEST IMAGES: Scalp close-up.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: TSH: Not available; Vitamin D: Not available; CBC with differential: Complete_Blood_Count (WBC: Normal for age, Hemoglobin: Normal for age, Platelets: Normal for age); Skin_Scraping: Microscopy (No signs of fungal infection), Culture (Negative for bacterial growth). Skin_Examination: Inspection (Erythematous patches observed on the scalp, forehead, and along the hairline), Palpation (Some patches covered by greasy yellow scales. No significant tenderness noted on palpation).

speaker: Doctor
text:
The test results showing greasy yellow scales on an erythematous scalp with a negative fungal culture and normal blood work are highly suggestive of seborrheic dermatitis, though we must rule out psoriasis given the family history. Can you tell me if there is any family history of atopic dermatitis (eczema) or asthma, and has this rash ever appeared on the face or ears?

REQUEST TEST: Skin biopsy of the affected area (if diagnosis remains unclear after clinical assessment).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin biopsy: Pending (requested due to diagnostic uncertainty between seborrheic dermatitis and psoriasis); Family History (Atopic Dermatitis/Asthma): Not specified in current data; Rash Distribution: Confirmed on scalp, forehead, and hairline; Scalp Appearance: Erythematous patches with greasy yellow scales; Microbiology: No fungal infection, no bacterial growth; Complete Blood Count: Normal for age (WBC, Hemoglobin, Platelets).

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic Dermatitis.

The clinical presentation of erythematous patches with greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead, combined with a negative fungal workup, normal blood counts, and an infant age group, strongly supports this diagnosis. The family history of psoriasis is noted but less likely given the specific "greasy" nature of the scales rather than "silvery" scales.
